title: First legitimate iPhone Air 2 dummy unit shows off key upgrade to spur sales
content:
Macworld

While everyone scrambles to find an iPhone Duo before January, those who choose to wait until 2027 to upgrade their iPhone may be in for a treat. For the first time, Apple will hold a second iPhone launch in the spring for the models that are still part of the iPhone 17 crop and one model is looking to get a huge upgrade.

In the spring, Apple is expected to release the iPhone 18 and 18e, as well as the iPhone Air 2. While we’re not expecting huge changes with either the iPhone 18 or 18e, the iPhone Air 2 has been rumored to get two key upgrades that held it back from being a sales success. And now it looks like we have proof of one of them.

Well-known and highly accurate leaker Sonny Dickson has posted images of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 dummy units that are used by case and accessory makers. While the overall design remains the same, we can clearly see a plateau at the top of the Air with holes for two cameras, matching the iPhone 18. We’ve heard for a while that Apple is planning to add a second ultra-wide camera to the Air 2, and this image seemingly confirms it.

Otherwise, the phones appear identical to their current counterparts, with the Air sporting a slightly larger display than the 18 (6.5 inches versus 6.3 inches) and both featuring the larger Dynamic Island. The iPhone 18 sill has the same vertical camera array in the left corner rather than the horizontal plateau of the Air. In addition to the extra camera, the iPhone Air 2 is also expected to gain a larger battery and a slightly thinner body.

Of note, Dickson calls this phone the iPhone 18 Air, which would be a name change. Even though the Air debuted as part of the iPhone 17 lineup, Apple opted to leave “17” off the name like the iPhone Duo. A name change would suggest that Apple plans on keeping the Air as part of the iPhone lineup and will upgrade it on an annual basis.

By all accounts, the iPhone Air was a sales flop, with users opting for the models with more cameras and bigger batteries over the Air’s unique ultra-thin design. However, Apple is looking to upgrade the follow-up model that addresses its two biggest complaints. The only other issue is the price. Apple bumped the starting price to $1,099 in September, which might be a little too high for a non-Pro phone that doesn’t fold. Here’s hoping it dips under $1,000 again in the spring.
